assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Restoring the hardcoded claim options or changing their order independently of the reordered taxonomy makes the expected literal order differ or raises before the assertion.
Removing the any-part contradiction instruction from the claim criterion removes the independently expected text.
Restoring a choice-only veto makes both positive veto assertions fail for a supports answer with contradiction probability 0.32; lowering the threshold through 0.04 makes the negative assertion fail.
Omitting the owning house-style audit erases the independently expected flawed finding, while a false positive on the clean entry breaks the clean assertion.
Removing audit input from score components makes clean and flawed scores equal; the source negative-audit-input.log records exactly this red result.

findings.text: follow-on: The new probability veto in jev_review.py:758-768 can reject a claim whose selected choice remains supports, but this runtime caller only collects selected contradictions, so its rejection reason omits the contradictory sentence needed for refinement.

follow-on: A caller can pass audit_report=None and still receive a numeric fitted score because missing audit components default to zero, so the score does not distinguish absent deterministic evidence from measured failing checks; current measurement calls pass reports.

follow-on: The 0.30 veto threshold was selected after the one missed planted contradiction, so 60/60 on that same subset verifies the repair but cannot independently support the replace verdict's veto generalisation; run a fresh planted or held-out contradiction cohort.
